exercises.title: Bài 1 · Why do we need insurance?
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
Life is full of uncertainty. A house can be damaged by a typhoon, a car can be stolen, and a family can suffer when a breadwinner becomes ill. Insurance is a way to reduce the financial effect of these events.

The idea is simple. Many people pay a small amount of money, called a premium, to an insurance company. The company, or insurer, collects all these premiums in a common fund. When something bad happens to one of the policyholders, the insurer pays for the loss from the fund. In this way, the risk is shared among many people. This is called pooling of risk.

The agreement between the insurer and the policyholder is written in a policy. It explains which risks are covered, how much the insurer will pay and what the policyholder must do. If there is a loss, the policyholder makes a claim. Insurance does not prevent accidents, but it gives financial protection and peace of mind. For companies, it also makes it possible to take business risks that would otherwise be too dangerous.

content.q: A premium is the money that the insurer pays after a loss.
content.why: Đoạn 2: premium là số tiền nhỏ khách hàng trả cho công ty bảo hiểm.

content.q: Insurance spreads the risk among many people.
content.why: Đoạn 2: gọi là pooling of risk.

content.q: The policy explains which risks are covered.
content.why: Đoạn 3: hợp đồng nêu rủi ro được bảo hiểm và mức chi trả.

content.q: Insurance prevents accidents from happening.
content.why: Đoạn 3: bảo hiểm không ngăn tai nạn, chỉ bảo vệ về tài chính.

content.q: What is a premium?
content.why: Đoạn 2: nhiều người trả một khoản nhỏ gọi là phí bảo hiểm.
opts: A payment made after a loss
A small amount of money paid to the insurer

content.q: Where does the insurer pay losses from?
content.why: Đoạn 2: quỹ chung từ phí bảo hiểm.
opts: From a common fund of premiums

content.q: What does the policy explain?
content.why: Đoạn 3: rủi ro được bảo hiểm, mức chi trả và nghĩa vụ của khách hàng.
opts: What is covered and how much the insurer will pay

content.q: How does insurance help companies?
content.why: Đoạn 3: giúp doanh nghiệp dám chấp nhận rủi ro kinh doanh.
opts: It makes it possible to take business risks.

exercises.title: Bài 2 · Hazard, peril and risk
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
People often use the words risk, peril and hazard as if they meant the same thing, but in insurance they are different. A peril is the cause of a loss, for example fire, flood, theft or an accident. A hazard is something that increases the chance or the size of a loss. A pile of paper near an electric heater is a hazard because it makes a fire more likely. Risk is the uncertainty about whether a loss will happen and how big it will be.

Insurers study these factors carefully. They use statistics to estimate the probability of each peril. A house in a flood area has a higher probability of flood damage than a house on a hill, so its premium is usually higher. Customers can help to reduce the risk. For example, a shop owner who installs smoke alarms or a car owner who parks in a safe garage may receive a discount.

Not every risk can be insured. The policyholder must have an insurable interest, which means that he or she would suffer a real financial loss. A person cannot insure a neighbour's house simply because he thinks it might burn down. Also, the loss must be accidental. Insurers do not pay if the policyholder causes the damage on purpose.

content.q: A peril is the cause of a loss.
content.why: Đoạn 1: peril là nguyên nhân gây tổn thất, ví dụ cháy, lũ, trộm.

content.q: A pile of paper near a heater is a peril.
content.why: Đoạn 1: đó là hazard, vì làm tăng khả năng cháy.

content.q: A house in a flood area usually has a higher premium.
content.why: Đoạn 2: xác suất ngập cao hơn nên phí thường cao hơn.

content.q: Insurers pay when the policyholder causes the damage on purpose.
content.why: Đoạn 3: tổn thất phải mang tính ngẫu nhiên; cố ý gây ra thì không được trả.

content.q: What is a hazard?
content.why: Đoạn 1: hazard làm tăng khả năng hoặc quy mô tổn thất.
opts: Something that increases the chance or size of a loss

content.q: How can customers reduce the risk?
content.why: Đoạn 2: lắp báo khói hoặc đỗ xe an toàn có thể được giảm phí.
opts: By installing smoke alarms or parking in a safe garage

content.q: What is insurable interest?
content.why: Đoạn 3: người mua phải chịu thiệt hại tài chính thực sự.
opts: A real financial loss if the damage happens

content.q: Why can't a person insure a neighbour's house?
content.why: Đoạn 3: không có quyền lợi có thể được bảo hiểm.

exercises.title: Bài 1 · Life and health insurance
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
Life insurance pays a sum of money to the family when the insured person dies. There are two main types. Term life covers the policyholder for a fixed period, for example twenty years, and it is usually cheap. Whole life covers the person for the whole of his or her life and also builds up a cash value, so it costs more.

Health insurance pays all or part of the cost of medical care. Inpatient cover pays for treatment in hospital, while outpatient cover pays for visits to the doctor. Some policies also include critical illness cover, which pays a lump sum if the policyholder is diagnosed with a serious disease such as cancer. This money can be used for treatment or to replace lost income.

Another product is the annuity. A person pays a large sum, or a series of payments, and then receives a regular income after retirement. As people live longer, annuities are becoming more popular. Before buying any of these policies, customers should compare the prices and benefits carefully, and they should check what is not covered.

content.q: Term life covers a person for a fixed period.
content.why: Đoạn 1: bảo hiểm có thời hạn, ví dụ hai mươi năm.

content.q: Whole life is usually cheaper than term life.
content.why: Đoạn 1: trọn đời có giá trị tích lũy nên chi phí cao hơn.

content.q: Outpatient cover pays for hospital stays.
content.why: Đoạn 2: inpatient trả cho nằm viện; outpatient trả cho khám bác sĩ.

content.q: Annuities give a regular income after retirement.
content.why: Đoạn 3: niên kim trả thu nhập định kỳ sau khi nghỉ hưu.

content.q: What does critical illness cover pay?
content.why: Đoạn 2: khoản tiền một lần khi được chẩn đoán bệnh nặng.
opts: Only the cost of a taxi
A lump sum if the policyholder is diagnosed with a serious disease
A monthly bonus for good health

content.q: Why is whole life more expensive?
content.why: Đoạn 1: bảo vệ trọn đời và tích lũy giá trị tiền mặt.
opts: It covers the whole life and builds up a cash value.

content.q: What should customers do before buying a policy?
content.why: Đoạn 3: so sánh giá, quyền lợi và kiểm tra điều khoản loại trừ.
opts: Compare prices and benefits and check what is not covered

content.q: Why are annuities becoming more popular?
content.why: Đoạn 3: người dân sống lâu hơn.

exercises.title: Bài 2 · Motor and property insurance
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
Motor insurance is one of the most common types of non-life insurance. In many countries, the law says that every driver must have at least third-party liability cover. This pays for injury or damage that the driver causes to other people, but it does not pay for the driver's own car. A comprehensive policy covers both. It pays for damage to the policyholder's vehicle after an accident, a fire or a theft.

Drivers who do not make a claim for a year receive a no-claims bonus, which reduces next year's premium. On the other hand, young drivers and drivers who have had many accidents usually pay more.

Property insurance protects homes and businesses. Buildings insurance covers the structure, such as the walls and the roof, while contents insurance covers furniture, electrical goods and other belongings. Typical perils are fire, storm, flood and theft. Business owners often add business interruption cover, which pays for lost income when a company must stop work after a fire or a flood. Property owners should always check the sum insured. If it is too low, the insurer may pay only part of the loss.

content.q: Third-party liability cover pays for the driver's own car.
content.why: Đoạn 1: nó chỉ trả cho thương tích hoặc thiệt hại gây ra cho người khác.

content.q: A no-claims bonus reduces next year's premium.
content.why: Đoạn 2: không bồi thường trong một năm thì phí năm sau giảm.

content.q: Buildings insurance covers furniture.
content.why: Đoạn 3: công trình bảo hiểm tường, mái; đồ đạc thuộc contents insurance.

content.q: Business interruption cover pays for lost income.
content.why: Đoạn 3: trả thu nhập bị mất khi công ty phải ngừng hoạt động.

content.q: What does third-party liability cover pay for?
content.why: Đoạn 1: thương tích hoặc thiệt hại cho người khác.
opts: Damage to the driver's own car
Injury or damage that the driver causes to other people

content.q: Who usually pays more for motor insurance?
content.why: Đoạn 2: người lái trẻ và người nhiều tai nạn thường trả nhiều hơn.
opts: Young drivers and drivers with many accidents

content.q: What does contents insurance cover?
content.why: Đoạn 3: đồ nội thất, đồ điện và tài sản khác.
opts: Furniture, electrical goods and other belongings

content.q: What may happen if the sum insured is too low?
content.why: Đoạn 3: công ty bảo hiểm có thể chỉ trả một phần.
opts: The insurer may pay only part of the loss.

exercises.title: Bài 1 · How underwriters decide
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
When a customer applies for insurance, the underwriter has to answer one question: should we accept this risk, and at what price? The process begins with the application form, in which the customer gives personal information. For life and health insurance, the applicant may also have to take a medical examination.

The underwriter studies the risk factors, such as age, occupation, health and lifestyle. A non-smoker is a lower risk than a smoker, and a clerk is a lower risk than a construction worker. If the risk is higher than normal, the underwriter can add a loading to the premium, apply an exclusion, or decline the application. If the risk is very low, the customer may receive a discount.

Honesty is essential. Insurance is based on the principle of utmost good faith, which means that the customer must disclose all important facts. If he or she hides a fact, this is called non-disclosure. When the insurer discovers it later, it may refuse a claim or cancel the policy. For this reason, applicants should read every question carefully and answer it truthfully.

content.q: For life insurance, the applicant may need a medical examination.
content.why: Đoạn 1: với bảo hiểm nhân thọ và sức khỏe, có thể phải khám sức khỏe.

content.q: A smoker is usually a lower risk than a non-smoker.
content.why: Đoạn 2: người không hút thuốc rủi ro thấp hơn.

content.q: An underwriter can add a loading to the premium.
content.why: Đoạn 2: nếu rủi ro cao hơn bình thường có thể thêm phụ phí.

content.q: Non-disclosure has no effect on claims.
content.why: Đoạn 3: công ty có thể từ chối bồi thường hoặc hủy hợp đồng.

content.q: What does the underwriter decide?
content.why: Đoạn 1: có nhận rủi ro hay không và với mức phí nào.
opts: Whether to accept the risk and at what price

content.q: Which of these are risk factors?
content.why: Đoạn 2: tuổi, nghề nghiệp, sức khỏe và lối sống.
opts: Colour and size of the form

content.q: What is utmost good faith?
content.why: Đoạn 3: khách hàng phải khai báo mọi thông tin quan trọng.
opts: The customer must disclose all important facts.

content.q: What can happen after non-disclosure is discovered?
content.why: Đoạn 3: từ chối bồi thường hoặc hủy hợp đồng.
opts: The insurer may refuse a claim or cancel the policy.

exercises.title: Bài 2 · Reading your policy
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
Most people never read their insurance policy until they need to make a claim, but this is a mistake. A policy has several parts. The schedule shows the personal details, the policy period, the sum insured and the premium. The policy wording explains the terms and conditions. The most important sections are the cover, the exclusions and the claims procedure.

The cover describes what the insurer will pay for. The exclusions list what is not covered. For example, a travel policy may exclude dangerous sports, and a health policy may exclude illnesses that the customer already had before the start date. Some policies have a waiting period, during which the customer cannot claim. Many also have a deductible, which means that the policyholder pays the first part of each claim.

If the customer's situation changes, the insurer may issue an endorsement, which is an official change to the policy. A rider can add an extra benefit, such as accidental death cover. After buying the policy, customers usually have a cooling-off period of a few weeks to change their mind and cancel without penalty. If they forget to pay the premium, many insurers allow a grace period before the policy lapses.

content.q: The schedule shows the sum insured and the policy period.
content.why: Đoạn 1: bảng chi tiết hợp đồng ghi thông tin cá nhân, thời hạn, số tiền bảo hiểm và phí.

content.q: An exclusion lists what the insurer will pay for.
content.why: Đoạn 2: exclusion liệt kê những gì không được bảo hiểm.

content.q: A rider can add an extra benefit.
content.why: Đoạn 3: điều khoản bổ sung thêm quyền lợi, ví dụ tử vong do tai nạn.

content.q: Customers can never cancel a policy after buying it.
content.why: Đoạn 3: thường có thời gian cân nhắc vài tuần để hủy không mất phí.

content.q: What does a deductible mean?
content.why: Đoạn 2: khách hàng tự chịu phần đầu của mỗi lần bồi thường.
opts: The policyholder pays the first part of each claim.

content.q: What may a travel policy exclude?
content.why: Đoạn 2: ví dụ môn thể thao nguy hiểm.

content.q: What is a cooling-off period?
content.why: Đoạn 3: vài tuần để đổi ý và hủy không mất phí.
opts: A time when the premium rises
A few weeks to cancel without penalty

content.q: What does an endorsement do?
content.why: Đoạn 3: sửa đổi chính thức hợp đồng khi hoàn cảnh thay đổi.
opts: It makes an official change to the policy.

exercises.title: Bài 1 · Making a claim: step by step
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
When a loss happens, the policyholder should act quickly. First, he must make the situation safe and try to prevent further damage. For example, if a pipe bursts, he should turn off the water. Then he should contact the insurer, usually by phone or online, and report the incident. Many policies require notification within a certain number of days.

Next, the policyholder fills in a claim form and sends evidence. This may include photographs, a police report, repair estimates and receipts. The insurer's claims handler checks the policy to see whether the event is covered. For larger losses, a loss adjuster visits the site, talks to witnesses and decides how much the loss is worth.

If the claim is accepted, the insurer pays the settlement or arranges for the repair. Depreciation may be deducted if the policy pays the actual cash value. If the claim is denied, the insurer must explain why in writing, and the customer can appeal. Throughout the process, the policyholder should keep copies of all documents and should not throw away the damaged items until the insurer has seen them.

content.q: The policyholder should try to prevent further damage.
content.why: Đoạn 1: trước hết giữ an toàn và ngăn thiệt hại thêm.

content.q: Notification is never required within a certain number of days.
content.why: Đoạn 1: nhiều hợp đồng yêu cầu thông báo trong số ngày nhất định.

content.q: A loss adjuster may visit the site for larger losses.
content.why: Đoạn 2: giám định viên đến hiện trường với tổn thất lớn.

content.q: The customer cannot appeal if the claim is denied.
content.why: Đoạn 3: khách hàng có thể khiếu nại.

content.q: Which of these is an example of evidence?
content.why: Đoạn 2: ảnh, biên bản công an, báo giá sửa chữa, hóa đơn.
opts: Photographs, a police report and receipts

content.q: What does the claims handler check?
content.why: Đoạn 2: xem sự kiện có thuộc phạm vi bảo hiểm không.
opts: Whether the event is covered by the policy

content.q: What must the insurer do if it denies a claim?
content.why: Đoạn 3: phải giải thích bằng văn bản.

content.q: What should the customer NOT do?
content.why: Đoạn 3: không vứt bỏ đồ hư hỏng trước khi công ty bảo hiểm xem.
opts: Throw away the damaged items before the insurer has seen them

exercises.title: Bài 2 · Detecting insurance fraud
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
Insurance fraud costs the industry billions of dollars every year, and honest customers pay for it through higher premiums. There are two main types. Soft fraud happens when a customer exaggerates a real claim, for example by adding items that were not damaged. Hard fraud means that the person invents or deliberately causes a loss, for example by burning a car and then reporting it as stolen.

Insurers have developed many methods to detect fraud. Claims handlers look for red flags: a claim that is made soon after the policy starts, an owner who cannot show any receipts, or a story that keeps changing. Computer systems compare new claims with a database of past claims and identify patterns that are unusual. Special investigators may interview witnesses and check social media.

When fraud is proved, the insurer refuses the claim and may cancel the policy. It can also report the case to the police, and the customer may go to prison. Insurers also try to prevent fraud by educating customers. Honest customers should remember a simple rule: describe the loss as it really happened, and give documents that are true.

content.q: Honest customers pay for fraud through higher premiums.
content.why: Đoạn 1: gian lận làm phí bảo hiểm tăng.

content.q: Soft fraud means that a person deliberately destroys property.
content.why: Đoạn 1: soft fraud là phóng đại yêu cầu có thật; cố ý gây ra tổn thất là hard fraud.

content.q: Computer systems can identify unusual patterns in claims.
content.why: Đoạn 2: hệ thống so sánh với cơ sở dữ liệu để phát hiện bất thường.

content.q: A person who commits fraud never goes to prison.
content.why: Đoạn 3: có thể bị báo công an và bị tù.

content.q: What is an example of hard fraud?
content.why: Đoạn 1: cố ý gây tổn thất rồi khai báo.
opts: Adding a few items to a real claim
Burning a car and then reporting it as stolen

content.q: Which of these is a red flag?
content.why: Đoạn 2: yêu cầu bồi thường ngay sau khi hợp đồng bắt đầu.
opts: A claim made soon after the policy starts
A customer who sends all receipts

content.q: What may the insurer do when fraud is proved?
content.why: Đoạn 3: từ chối bồi thường và có thể hủy hợp đồng.
opts: Refuse the claim and cancel the policy

content.q: How do insurers try to prevent fraud?
content.why: Đoạn 3: bằng cách giáo dục khách hàng.

exercises.title: Bài 1 · Reinsurance: insurance for insurers
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
Imagine that an insurer has sold fire policies for thousands of buildings in one city. If a huge fire or an earthquake happens, the company may have to pay thousands of claims at the same time. A single catastrophe could destroy its capital. To avoid this danger, insurers buy reinsurance.

Reinsurance is insurance for insurance companies. The original insurer, called the ceding company, passes part of its risk to a reinsurer in exchange for a share of the premium. Under a treaty, the reinsurer automatically accepts a whole portfolio of risks, for example all property policies of a certain type. For very large single risks, such as an oil refinery or a satellite, the company may arrange a separate agreement.

Reinsurance has several benefits. It protects the insurer's capital and keeps its results stable. It also allows the insurer to accept larger risks and to sell more policies. Because a major catastrophe can hit many countries, the biggest reinsurers are international. They spread their risk over many regions and many types of insurance, which is called diversification. In recent years, reinsurers have also developed catastrophe bonds, which sell part of the risk to investors in the capital market.

content.q: A ceding company passes part of its risk to a reinsurer.
content.why: Đoạn 2: công ty nhượng chuyển một phần rủi ro cho công ty tái bảo hiểm.

content.q: Reinsurance can protect the insurer's capital.
content.why: Đoạn 3: tái bảo hiểm bảo vệ vốn và giữ kết quả ổn định.

content.q: A treaty covers only one single risk.
content.why: Đoạn 2: hiệp ước tự động nhận cả danh mục rủi ro.

content.q: The biggest reinsurers operate only in one region.
content.why: Đoạn 3: các công ty tái bảo hiểm lớn mang tính quốc tế.

content.q: Why do insurers buy reinsurance?
content.why: Đoạn 1: một thảm họa có thể phá hủy vốn.
opts: To avoid a single catastrophe destroying their capital

content.q: What does the reinsurer receive?
content.why: Đoạn 2: nhận một phần phí bảo hiểm.

content.q: What is diversification?
content.why: Đoạn 3: dàn trải rủi ro theo nhiều khu vực và loại hình.
opts: Spreading risk over many regions and types of insurance

content.q: What do catastrophe bonds do?
content.why: Đoạn 3: bán một phần rủi ro cho nhà đầu tư.
opts: They sell part of the risk to investors.

exercises.title: Bài 2 · Agents, brokers and risk management
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
Insurance products reach customers through different distribution channels. An agent usually represents one insurer and receives a commission for each policy sold. A broker, on the other hand, works for the customer and compares the products of many insurers. Another channel is bancassurance, where banks sell insurance in their branches, and more and more customers buy directly on the Internet or through mobile apps developed by insurtech companies.

Companies also need to manage their own risks. Risk management usually has four steps. First, the company identifies its risks, such as fire, theft, cyber attacks or the loss of an important manager. Second, it measures how likely each risk is and how much damage it could cause. Third, it decides how to respond. It can avoid the risk, reduce it, retain it, or transfer it. Transferring the risk, often by buying insurance, is only one of these options. Finally, the company monitors the results and adjusts its plan.

A company's risk appetite, that is, how much risk it is willing to accept, depends on its size and its financial strength. A large company may prefer self-insurance for small, frequent losses, and buy insurance only against rare but very expensive events.

content.q: A broker usually represents only one insurer.
content.why: Đoạn 1: đại lý thường đại diện một công ty; môi giới làm việc cho khách hàng và so sánh nhiều công ty.

content.q: Bancassurance means selling insurance through banks.
content.why: Đoạn 1: ngân hàng bán bảo hiểm tại chi nhánh.

content.q: Buying insurance is the only way to respond to a risk.

exercises.title: Bài 1 · Handling a customer complaint
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
A complaint is a chance to keep a customer, not just a problem. Mrs Mai bought a travel policy, but when her bag was stolen on holiday, the insurer rejected her claim. She phoned the hotline and spoke to an adviser. The adviser listened carefully, apologised for the stress and wrote down the policy number and the details of the complaint. He promised that a senior colleague would call her within two working days.

The next day, the complaints team reviewed the case. They found that the exclusion in the policy did not apply because Mrs Mai had reported the theft to the local police immediately. The manager called her, explained the mistake and offered to pay the claim in full. She also sent an email to confirm everything in writing.

Mrs Mai said that she was satisfied and renewed her policy. Good complaint handling has four steps: listen, apologise, investigate and put things right. If the customer is still not happy, he or she can contact the ombudsman, an independent body that investigates unresolved complaints. Insurers must keep a record of every complaint and use the information to improve their services.

content.q: Mrs Mai's claim was first rejected.
content.why: Đoạn 1: công ty bảo hiểm từ chối yêu cầu của bà Mai.

content.q: The adviser promised to call her within two weeks.
content.why: Đoạn 1: một đồng nghiệp cấp cao sẽ gọi trong vòng hai ngày làm việc.

content.q: The insurer found that the exclusion did not apply.
content.why: Đoạn 2: bà đã báo công an ngay nên điều khoản loại trừ không áp dụng.

content.q: Mrs Mai cancelled her policy after the complaint.
content.why: Đoạn 3: bà hài lòng và tái tục hợp đồng.

content.q: What did the adviser write down?
content.why: Đoạn 1: số hợp đồng và chi tiết khiếu nại.
opts: The policy number and the details of the complaint

content.q: Why did the exclusion not apply?
content.why: Đoạn 2: bà báo công an ngay lập tức.
opts: She had reported the theft to the police immediately.

content.q: What are the four steps of good complaint handling?
content.why: Đoạn 3: lắng nghe, xin lỗi, điều tra, khắc phục.
opts: Listen, apologise, investigate and put things right

content.q: Who can investigate unresolved complaints?
content.why: Đoạn 3: cơ quan giải quyết khiếu nại độc lập.

exercises.title: Bài 2 · Regulation and ethics
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
Insurance is a business of trust. Customers pay their premiums today and hope that the insurer will pay their claim in the future. For this reason, the industry is strictly regulated. In every country, a regulator gives licences to insurers, checks that they have enough capital to pay claims, and protects customers from unfair practices.

Insurance staff must also follow a code of conduct. They must treat customers fairly, explain products clearly and avoid mis-selling. For example, an agent should not sell a very expensive policy to a customer who does not need it just to earn a higher commission. If the agent has a conflict of interest, he must tell the customer.

Insurers also have legal duties to prevent crime. Under anti-money-laundering rules, they must check the identity of new customers, which is known as KYC, and report suspicious transactions. Data protection laws require them to keep personal information safe and to use it only for the purpose for which it was collected. Medical and financial details are especially sensitive, so confidentiality is essential.

Compliance officers check that the company follows all these rules. A company that breaks them may receive a heavy fine or even lose its licence.

content.q: A regulator gives licences to insurers.
content.why: Đoạn 1: cơ quan quản lý cấp giấy phép và kiểm tra vốn.

content.q: Agents may sell expensive policies to earn more commission, whatever the customer needs.
content.why: Đoạn 2: đó là mis-selling, bị cấm.

content.q: Insurers must report suspicious transactions.
content.why: Đoạn 3: theo quy định phòng chống rửa tiền.

content.q: A company that breaks the rules never receives a penalty.
content.why: Đoạn 4: có thể bị phạt nặng hoặc mất giấy phép.

content.q: What does KYC mean in practice?
content.why: Đoạn 3: kiểm tra danh tính khách hàng mới.
opts: Checking the identity of new customers

content.q: What must an agent do if there is a conflict of interest?
content.why: Đoạn 2: phải thông báo cho khách hàng.

content.q: Why is confidentiality essential?
content.why: Đoạn 3: thông tin y tế và tài chính rất nhạy cảm.
opts: Medical and financial details are very sensitive.

content.q: What does a compliance officer do?
content.why: Đoạn 4: kiểm tra công ty tuân thủ mọi quy định.
opts: Checks that the company follows all the rules
